block.prompt:
Your exchange partner from England had to leave the room and missed most of the programme. In English, write them a short message (about 80–100 words) that tells them:
- what the programme was about
- the example of Hallstatt (with one or two key facts)
- the TWO main sides of the argument you heard.

Choose only the information your partner really needs — you cannot include everything, so leave out the small details and keep the message clear and useful.
block.answer_key: Model message (approx. 95 words): “Hi! You missed a good radio programme about ‚overtourism' — when too many tourists overwhelm a beautiful place. The main example was Hallstatt in Austria: fewer than 800 people live there, but up to 10,000 visitors can come on one summer day, and locals are being priced out. There were two sides. Some people want to limit or change visitor numbers to protect residents. Others say tourism keeps these villages alive and the real answer is better management — spreading visitors out, not turning them away. The big question was: who does a place belong to?” Accept any coherent 80–100-word briefing that selects the key facts and both positions and leaves out minor detail.
block.acceptable_reasoning: Es handelt sich um Sprachmittlung: Bewertet werden die AUSWAHL relevanter Informationen, die Adressatenorientierung (verständlich für die Partnerin/den Partner) und sprachliche Klarheit — NICHT Vollständigkeit. Wer alle Details übernimmt, hat die Aufgabe (‚choose only what your partner needs') verfehlt.

levels: Only the key facts and both sides included; minor detail rightly left out
Mostly relevant but some clutter or a missing key point
Poor selection: overloaded with detail or key points missing
Both positions communicated clearly and fairly
Both present but one is unclear
Clear, well-organised message suited to the reader; word count met
Understandable; small issues with flow or length
Hard to follow or badly off the word count
Mostly accurate; errors do not affect meaning

watch_outs: Sprachmittlung ist NICHT Übersetzung und nicht ‚alles wiedergeben': Wer den gesamten Hörtext nacherzählt, verfehlt das Auswahlkriterium. Weglassen ist Teil der Leistung.
Beide Seiten des Arguments müssen vorkommen — viele geben nur EINE Position wieder. Explizit einfordern.
Wortzahl (80–100) im Blick behalten: zu kurz → Kerninfos fehlen; zu lang → Auswahl misslungen. Register darf informell sein (Nachricht an eine:n Freund:in).
